svg.text: Many teenagers go to bed late and get up early, and the result is a generation of
tired students. Doctors say that people aged 14 to 17 need between eight and ten hours
of sleep a night, but surveys show that most of them get only about six or seven.
Why does this happen? One reason is that during the teenage years the body clock
changes, so young people naturally feel sleepy later in the evening. Another reason is
technology: many teens scroll through their phones in bed, and the blue light from the
screen makes it harder to fall asleep.
Some schools have decided to start lessons later. In one town in the north of England,
where classes began at 10 a.m. instead of 8:30, students' exam results improved and
Experts advise teenagers to switch off their phones an hour before bedtime, to go to
bed at the same time every day and to avoid coffee in the evening.
